title: Krishna's two natures
hookLine: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, the sense of I: in the Gita, Krishna calls the whole list his nature, and then says there's more
carry: even the mind is prakriti, god's nature

lines: MIND, INTELLECT, THE SENSE OF I.
THIS IS MY NATURE. THE LOWER ONE.
cards: Intellect. The sense of I. In the seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna lists these one after another, the way you'd unpack a box onto a table.
The ground under your feet, the thoughts in your head, even the feeling of being someone: all on one list. Then he says: this is my nature. Mine.

teach.b: Here are the verses, in paraphrase.

teach.h: EVEN MIND AND THE SENSE OF I.
teach.b: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I: this is my prakriti, my nature, divided eightfold. That is the lower.
Know my other, higher nature, the life in things, by which this whole world is upheld. All beings come from these two, as from a womb. I am where the whole world begins, and where it dissolves.
First, the word. Prakriti: nature, the stuff and the shaping of things. Krishna calls it his.
Matter isn't the enemy of the divine here; it belongs to God. Second, what's on the lower list. Mind, intellect and the sense of I are there too.

The thoughts you're thinking right now are, in the Gita's picture, part of nature, moving like weather. Many teachers draw the lesson plainly: your racing thoughts are prakriti at work, not the deepest you.

teach.h: THE HIGHER NATURE HOLDS THE WORLD UP.
teach.b: Third, the higher nature: the life that holds the world up. Some readers hear every living being in it; others hear the spark of awareness in each one. Either way, the world doesn't just sit there.

teach.h: THE WEEK: A VERSE, A STRAW, A SEEING.
teach.b: Fourth, the week. Here the Gita speaks through Krishna; in the days ahead, a goddess text takes up this same word, prakriti, in her own voice. Look back.
Parvati's tapas, and her kitchen in Kashi. Ramakrishna's snake. Shiva who can't stir without Shakti.
A blade of grass, and Uma who named the power behind it. Seekers who saw God's power hidden in the world.

teach.h: ALL OF THIS IS MINE, AND THERE IS MORE.
teach.b: And now Krishna: all of this is mine, and there is more.

how: The Bhagavad Gita's seventh chapter is studied and chanted in homes and Gita classes, and teachers use its two natures, lower and higher, to explain how the divine relates to the world.

games.q: what does “shakti as a philosophy” mean?
o: nature itself as divine power, from earth to mind
a list of the elements used in temple rituals
a war between nature and the soul inside it

games.q: the week of Shakti — tap the pairs.
p: a lower nature, and a higher

s: in the Gita's list, the mind is part of nature
mind, intellect and the sense of I are on the lower list, with earth and water.
Krishna calls matter something apart from himself
he calls it his prakriti, his own nature.
the higher nature, says the Gita, holds the world up
the life in things, by which this world is upheld.

games.q: you're Arjuna. Krishna lists earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I, and calls it all his nature. what does he say next?
o: that this is everything there is.
that this is the lower nature, and he has a higher one.
that only the mind is real.
games.why: this is the lower, he says. know my other, higher nature, the life by which this world is upheld.

practice: Walk Krishna's list slowly, one breath each: earth, your weight on the seat; water, the wet of the mouth; fire, warm hands; air, the breath; space, the room; mind, the next thought; intellect, the part that names it; the sense of I.
Then rest in whatever is aware of the whole list. If you pray, you can offer the list back in the words you use.

wordCard.voice: Shakti as a philosophy. In the Gita, earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I make up the lower nature, and a higher one holds the world up.

orig.note: Sanskrit: prakriti, nature. In the Gita, Krishna calls his nature lower and higher.

carryVoice: Your line: even the mind is prakriti, God's nature. A racing mind is nature moving. Rest well.
